# Configuration inventory

<!-- Refresh: `uv run python scripts/config_inventory.py > docs/configuration.md` -->

83 environment variables, read from `src/tessera/settings.py`.

**Naming.** The canonical form is `TESSERA_<BLOCK>__<FIELD>` (double-underscore nested delimiter, keyed on the *composite field name*). Each nested block ALSO has its own `env_prefix` (a legacy second path). The trap: `observability` is exposed as `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__X` (canonical) or `TESSERA_OBS_X` (its block prefix) — but `TESSERA_OBS__X` (abbreviated prefix + `__`) matches neither and is silently ignored.

| `TESSERA_POSTGRES__POOL_MIN_SIZE` | `1` | Connection-pool bounds (retrieval.store.get_pool). Conservative for a single local process. Per-environment guidance (audit P1.3): dev / on-prem single instance : 1 / 10 — one process, few concurrent turns. e2e (Playwright, prod build)  : many pages hit one backend; max 10 STARVES under load (the proven e2e famine). Keep the suite at low worker count (playwright.config workers=1 already does) OR raise pool_max_size (~20) for parallel runs. CI / staging / production     : size to the Cloud SQL max_connections budget — pool_max_size * instance_count must stay under it; 10-20/instance is a sane start. | PostgresSettings |

Enrichment, never the store. The default ``none`` is the honesty invariant: with no provider configured the badge can NEVER read "Scellé" (the NoOp provider cannot mint a token). | `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__PROFILE` | `on_prem` | -- Frontier observability (ADR 0010) ----------------------------------- Which observability backend stack this process targets. Independent of ``deployment_mode``: an on-prem app may still ship traces to GCP, or a Cloud Run app may export to a self-hosted Phoenix. ``on_prem`` → OTLP to the local OpenTelemetry Collector (fanning out to Phoenix / Langfuse); ``gcp`` → Cloud Trace plus managed backends. | ObservabilitySettings |

| `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__CONTENT_CAPTURE` | `False` | Opt-in capture of prompt/completion *content* as span events (OTel GenAI convention). Off by default — content is sensitive in banking, so it is screened before it is ever attached (ADR 0010, idea #4). | ObservabilitySettings |
| `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__DATA_RESIDENCY` | `eu` | Data-residency tag attached to every span as a resource attribute and used by the Collector to route EU-only (ADR 0010, idea #3). | ObservabilitySettings |
| `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__JUDGE_MODEL` | `(unset)` | LLM-as-judge model for online evaluation; None → the cheap summary backend (the sovereign local Llama on the on-prem path). (ADR 0010, Phase 4.) | ObservabilitySettings |
| `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__ONLINE_EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` | `0.1` | Fraction of un-flagged turns scored online; flagged turns are always scored (tiered, cost-aware online eval — idea #6). | ObservabilitySettings |
| `TESSERA_OBSERVABILITY__CANARY_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` | `False` | ADR 0019 §I4 — the scheduled-canary master switch (the operator's activation). OFF by default: even with a manifest cadence declared, no synthetic turn fires until the operator opts in (synthetic traffic hits the real agent + LLM — a deliberate act, never implicit). The scheduler is always WIRED (it idles under this flag), so flipping it is go-and-observe, never a latent provisioned-but-silent trap (the Hica-seal off-chrono lesson). | ObservabilitySettings |

| `TESSERA_API__SESSION_SIGNING_KEY` | `(unset)` | HMAC key for the signed customer-session cookie (ADR 0008/0009). Resolved from the environment — in production from GCP Secret Manager, mounted as TESSERA_API_SESSION_SIGNING_KEY — and NEVER committed. When unset (local dev / CI) the session layer falls back to a process-ephemeral key. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__OPERATOR_ASSERTION_SIGNING_KEY` | `(unset)` | HMAC key for the signed OPERATOR assertion (ADR 0010 Phase B). The Next BFF mints the assertion after verifying a next-auth operator session; the agent verifies it here to derive AuthState.OPERATOR. Because mint (front) and verify (agent) live in *different* processes, both MUST share this exact value via env / GCP Secret Manager (TESSERA_API_OPERATOR_ASSERTION_SIGNING_KEY) — there is no ephemeral fallback (a per-process key could never match across the trust boundary). Required in production (fail-closed); when unset in dev/CI the operator path is simply inert (no assertion ever verifies). | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__TLS_TERMINATED` | `True` | -- Security hardening (ADR 0020) --------------------------------------- TLS is terminated by Cloud Run; an on-prem reverse proxy may not, in which case HSTS must stay off. Drives the security-headers middleware. | APISettings |

| `TESSERA_API__EXPOSE_DOCS` | `True` | Interactive API docs (/docs) and the OpenAPI schema (/openapi.json). On by default for local dev, always forced off in production. Set False to also close them on a non-prod agent that is nonetheless reachable from the internet (e.g. exposed via a tunnel) — they leak the full route surface. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `True` | Rate limiting (the `limits` lib). Defaults are conservative; tune per env. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_CHAT` | `20/hour` | Per-session limit on POST /chat (keyed by the X-Session-Id cookie the front forwards). "20/hour" embodies the "20 per session" budget for a public, login-less demo; raise it for trusted environments. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_GLOBAL` | `200/hour` | Hard global ceiling on POST /chat across ALL sessions — bounds total LLM cost even if sessions are farmed. Checked in addition to the per-session limit. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_READ` | `120/minute` | — | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_URI` | `(unset)` | Optional shared store (e.g. "redis://host:6379") for correct limits across multiple Cloud Run instances; in-memory (per-instance) when unset. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__TRUST_FORWARDED_HEADERS` | `False` | When True, derive the rate-limit identity from forwarded headers (X-Forwarded-For / CF-Connecting-IP) instead of the immediate peer. Enable only behind a trusted proxy (Next, nginx, cloudflared) that sets them. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__RATE_LIMIT_INVOKE` | `12/minute` | POST /agents/{id}/invoke — the declared invocation seam (ADR 0019). Bounded PER AGENT (binding) and PER ROLE (the operator surface), so an operator cannot hammer an agent's test endpoint. A purpose-built limit, tighter than the generic read one. | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__INVOKE_MAX_CONCURRENT` | `4` | Max concurrent in-flight invocations of one agent per role — protects a foreign runtime from a thundering herd of operator test turns. In-process (per instance; a shared rate_limit_storage_uri only backs the rate window, not this counter). | APISettings |
| `TESSERA_API__MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `256000` | Global request-body ceiling, in addition to per-field Pydantic caps. | APISettings |
